schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE event
(
    event_id   TEXT
        constraint event_pk
            primary key,
    event_name TEXT,
    event_date TEXT,
    type       TEXT,
    notes      TEXT,
    location   TEXT,
    status     TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE major
(
    major_id   TEXT
        constraint major_pk
            primary key,
    major_name TEXT,
    department TEXT,
    college    TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE zip_code
(
    zip_code    INTEGER
        constraint zip_code_pk
            primary key,
    type        TEXT,
    city        TEXT,
    county      TEXT,
    state       TEXT,
    short_state TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE "attendance"
(
    link_to_event  TEXT,
    link_to_member TEXT,
    primary key (link_to_event, link_to_member),
    foreign key (link_to_event) references event(event_id),
    foreign key (link_to_member) references member(member_id)
);

CREATE TABLE "budget"
(
    budget_id     TEXT
            primary key,
    category      TEXT,
    spent         REAL,
    remaining     REAL,
    amount        INTEGER,
    event_status  TEXT,
    link_to_event TEXT,
    foreign key (link_to_event) references event(event_id)
);

CREATE TABLE "expense"
(
    expense_id          TEXT
            primary key,
    expense_description TEXT,
    expense_date        TEXT,
    cost                REAL,
    approved            TEXT,
    link_to_member      TEXT,
    link_to_budget      TEXT,
    foreign key (link_to_budget) references budget(budget_id),
    foreign key (link_to_member) references member(member_id)
);

CREATE TABLE "income"
(
    income_id      TEXT
        constraint income_pk
            primary key,
    date_received  TEXT,
    amount         INTEGER,
    source         TEXT,
    notes          TEXT,
    link_to_member TEXT,
    foreign key (link_to_member) references member(member_id)
);

CREATE TABLE "member"
(
    member_id     TEXT
        constraint member_pk
            primary key,
    first_name    TEXT,
    last_name     TEXT,
    email         TEXT,
    position      TEXT,
    t_shirt_size  TEXT,
    phone         TEXT,
    zip           INTEGER,
    link_to_major TEXT,
    foreign key (link_to_major) references major(major_id),
    foreign key (zip) references zip_code(zip_code)
);
q1: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.amount = 50 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T2.income_id) FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN income AS T2 ON T1.member_id = T2.link_to_member WHERE T1.position = 'Member' AND T1.t_shirt_size = 'Medium'
q2: SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.amount = 50 THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T1.member_id) FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN income AS T2 ON T1.member_id = T2.link_to_member WHERE T1.t_shirt_size = 'Medium' AND T1.position = 'Member'

q2_prompt_sql: SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.amount = 50 THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T1.member_id) FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN income AS T2 ON T1.member_id = T2.link_to_member WHERE T1.t_shirt_size = 'Medium' AND T1.position = 'Member'
counterexample: INSERT INTO member (member_id, position, t_shirt_size) VALUES ('M001', 'Member', 'Medium'); INSERT INTO income (income_id, amount, link_to_member) VALUES ('I001', 50, 'M001'), ('I002', 100, 'M001');
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because they count the number of incomes differently. Q1 counts the number of incomes where the amount is 50, while Q2 counts the number of members who have at least one income of 50. The difference arises when a member has multiple incomes, and one of them is 50.
counterexample_dsp: Create a member with two incomes: one of 50 and another of 100. Q1 will count this as 50% (1 out of 2), while Q2 will count this as 100% (1 out of 1).
